Story definition and product state are current documentation. Acceptance needs a criterion; Git keeps earlier

g.text: Current story definition
Complete content is edited in place under a stable identity. Git
retains committed earlier definitions; current writers do not
append Saga revisions.
Current product state
Proposed, accepted, deferred, rejected and retired describe
product intent. State and reason edit the current record and
obey allowed transitions.
No hidden winner
Concurrent edits to the same current file use Git conflicts.
Unresolved legacy content/state stays ambiguous and cannot be
silently migrated.
Resolve content in Git
Combine conflicting branch intent explicitly with Git,
preserving earlier commits. Legacy normalization refuses
ambiguity; it never asks current authors for Saga parent IDs.
Acceptance guard
Setting accepted is rejected if the current story has no
acceptance criterion; no invalid accepted state is published.
Criterion-level currency
Relations survive unrelated story edits when criterion bytes are
unchanged, but rewording or removing that criterion makes the
pin stale.

svg.text: Stable identities · exact evidence pins · Git-owned committed history
